To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ultimate load decreases with increasing corrosion parameters.
the ultimate load of corroded angle members decreases in the case of the same cross-section, and increases in the case of different cross-section, as compared to the non-corroded case.
the ultimate load capacity decreases with the increase of the corrosion parameters, but this tendency is not linear.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical study of the behaviour of corroding steel angle compression members.
a study of the behaviour of corroding steel angle section members under compression.
the effects of the corrosion on the behaviour of steel angle section compression members.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
corrosion is the main factor of the decrease of the load carrying capacity of the members.
corrosion decreases the ultimate load of steel angle section members.
the ultimate load of the corroded members decreases in the case of all the cross-section types and all the slenderness ratios.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the corrosion has a great effect on the ultimate load.

the ultimate load of a corroded angle member is reduced by about 50% compared to that of the intact member, and the ultimate load of the member is reduced with increasing corrosion depth, increasing corrosion area, and with decreasing slenderness.
the corrosion has an adverse effect on the structural elements under centric compression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ultimate load of the members is decreased by the corrosion, and the slenderness has an increasing effect on the decreasing tendency.
the corrosion of the steel members can be a major problem in the design of steel structures.
the corrosion of steel angle compression members is a serious issue and the design of such members should take it into account.
